findings.finding: Discount-priced convertible and ATM supply is unfinished and can hit the tape on 2026-10-01. Astor can convert at 70% of the lowest 20-day VWAP, below any bounce price, into a registered and effective resale line, and the A.G.P. ATM stays open with 80% of its proceeds pledged to repaying the note.
findings.mechanism_in_window: Conversion is at the lender's option on any trading day and the resale registration has been effective since 2026-09-17. The ATM can draw on 10-01 with no further filing. The first weekly installments (Mondays from 09-21) are already running, so the holder is converting now and has not started later. Every share converted at 70% of the lowest VWAP is profitable to sell straight away on 10-01.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's September sequence: every one of the 12 drops since 09-10 closed lower the next day (-27.54, -12.40, -7.31, -2.46, -11.49, -7.79, -4.93, -10.37, -33.88, -5.00, -23.68, -6.55). That is the whole period in which this note and the resale line were live. Own 3-year history: median next close -2.51%, 36.9% up, n=271.
findings.why_not_priced: The price has taken today's selling, not tomorrow's. A conversion priced 30% or more below the lowest VWAP gives the holder a reason to sell at any price above the conversion price, so a close that held this supply would be at or below the conversion price, around $0.95 against a spot of $1.355. The note's principal of about $2.1m, plus the other Astor tranches, converts into more shares than the roughly 1.01m now outstanding. The 4.99% cap slows that and does not stop it.
